draft.title: Management skills
card: Interpersonal skills
Skills used to work well with people, such as motivating a team, building trust and handling conflict.
Communication
Getting information across clearly and listening to others, in speech, in writing and in meetings.
Decision-making and problem-solving
Decision-making is choosing between options. Problem-solving is finding the cause of an issue and a way to fix it.
Planning and adapting
Managers look ahead and set a course. They also change it when conditions change, such as a supplier closing or a drop in sales.
draft.remember: Good managers combine people skills with clear thinking, and they adjust when things change.

a.q: A manager calmly sorts out an argument between two staff and keeps both on the team. Which skill is she mainly using?
a.why: Handling conflict and keeping staff working well together is an interpersonal skill. Problem-solving is tempting, but that skill is about finding the cause of an issue and fixing it, not about working well with people.
a.clue: Think about skills used to work well with people.

b.q: Sam runs a bike shop in Bendigo. His main supplier suddenly closes, so he quickly finds two new suppliers and changes his order dates. Which skill is Sam showing most?
b.why: Sam changes his plans when conditions change, which is adapting. Setting long-term goals is tempting because it is part of planning, but Sam is changing a plan, not setting one.
b.clue: Look at what changed, and how Sam responded.
